topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture themes on cancer evolution, the role of the microenvironment, and the intended learning outcomes.

topics.label: Clonal Expansion and Darwinian Selection in Premalignant Tissues
topics.groupedBecause: It examines how sequential driver mutations confer competitive fitness advantages to drive clonal expansion in tissues prior to full malignant transformation.

topics.label: Epigenetic Regulation of Tumor Transformation
topics.groupedBecause: It demonstrates how transient chromatin and transcriptional remodeling can trigger malignant transformation independently of genetic mutations.

topics.label: Cell of Origin and Cancer Stem Cell Hierarchies
topics.groupedBecause: They evaluate how normal tissue differentiation hierarchies and inherent stemness properties influence which cell types are capable of initiating cancer.

topics.label: Environmental Promoters and Inflammatory Signaling in Tumor Progression
topics.groupedBecause: They explain how chronic inflammation and environmental stimuli act as tumor promoters by reprogramming mutated cells into stem-like states.

topics.label: Microenvironmental Support in Established Tumors and Therapeutic Strategies
topics.groupedBecause: It highlights the reliance of established tumors on supportive stromal environments and the therapeutic opportunities of targeting these non-cancerous components.

topics.label: Technological Approaches for Mapping Tumor Evolution and Spatial Biology
topics.groupedBecause: It details the computational, sequencing, and spatial profiling methods used to reconstruct tumor evolutionary trajectories and cellular interactions.

topics.label: Conclusion and Synthesis of Cancer Evolution
topics.groupedBecause: They synthesize the interplay between mutations, epigenetic plasticity, cell of origin, and microenvironmental forces in cancer progression, and conclude the lecture.
